newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 16.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 16.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
PARIS - French advertising agency Publicis Conseil says it wins kitchen utensil maker Tefal's worldwide advertising budget in competition with other agencies. (Reuter)
PARIS - French mattress maker Epeda embarks on a new phase of its communication with advertising agency Australie, after running a campaign focusing on hygiene and safety. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - The number of advertising pages carried in French magazines rose 9.8 percent in January and February of this year compared with the same two-month period last year, according to a monthly report published by advertising space specialist Mediapolis. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says it filed suit in Paris Commercial Court to obtain the forced execution of a contract it signed with Monarchy Enterprises for rights to New Regency films. The suit was filed after rival TPS announced it signed an exclusive deal with Regency. (Reuter)
PARIS - France Telecom says its Wanadoo computer online service had 35,000 paying subscribers after one year of existence. The number was rising by more than 6,000 per month, it says.
(Reuter)
PARIS - Canal Plus says it signs an exclusive deal with Miramax Film Corp. for pay television and pay-per-view television rights of upcoming films produced by the studio. (Reuter)
PARIS - Canal Plus says turnover rose 11.2 percent in the first quarter to 2.95 billion francs ($514.8 million). (Reuter)

PARIS - The Association des Villes Cablees (Association of Cabled Towns) says there were 1.52 million subscribers to the cable television basic service at March 30, 1997, up from 1.36 million a year earlier. (Les Echos)
BRAND NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Douwe Egberts France says it raises retail coffee prices by 1.50 francs per 250 grams of arabica coffee and by 65 centimes for each pack of robusta coffee, with immediate effect. The French unit of Dutch coffee roaster Douwe Egberts, a unit of Sara Lee Corp, controls 15 percent of the domestic coffee market. (Reuter)

PARIS - Orangina is about to launch in France a plastic version of the famous round Orangina glass bottle, after introducing the packaging in foreign markets three years ago. (Advertising Age's Daily World Wire).
PARIS - Coca-Cola and Danone are launching in France the new Minute Maid Premium, a juice packaged in cartons, with a TV campaign by Leo Burnett. (Advertising Age's Daily World Wire).
PARIS - French industrial activity should continue to pick up in the coming months, but a drop is expected in the car industry, the Bank of France says in its April survey of industrialists.
(Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
For further information and news, see Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing. And visit us on the Internet at http://www.Bizinfo.reuters.com
